author: Dalton Wright Sports Writer
title: Buckhannon-Upshur eager to turn playoff berth into building block for sustained success | West Virginia High School Sports | wvnews.com
text:
BUCKHANNON, W.Va. — Each season of the coach Sloan Baisden era has seen the Buckhannon-Upshur football program raise the bar and that momentum has shown no signs of slowing entering this fall.
After going winless during coach Baisden’s debut season, the Buccaneers improved to 2-9 last fall and secured their first Class AAAA playoff berth since 2016.
“We like to drive home our Standard Living mantra and our players have been great at buying in,” coach Baisden said. “We take that mindset into every aspect of our program, from playing on the field, practice time and weight room sessions to the classroom and the community.”
That growing investment from the players began to manifest itself last fall, giving coach Baisden tangible evidence that the program is headed in the right direction.
“It is always nice getting into the win column and many of our losses were very competitive,” coach Baisden said. “Showing them how far we came from that first year gives us hope, makes it easier to get players to buy in, take ownership and work to get a couple more wins each year moving forward.”
Continuing its upward trajectory will require Buckhannon-Upshur to overcome the departure of one of the most productive players in program history in four-year starting quarterback Dawson Tenney.
The now-University of Charleston freshman signal-caller closed his final campaign as a Buccaneer with All-Big 10 Blue Division and second-team Class AAAA All-State honors after setting school records with 2,253 all-purpose yards and 23 total touchdowns before finishing his career as the program’s all-time leader in total yards, passing yards, pass attempts and total touchdowns.
“Dawson’s statistics speak for themselves, but losing him as a vocal leader is another challenge in itself,” coach Baisden said. “His presence in the weight room, on the practice field, on the sideline or in the huddle will be hard to fill. His absence leaves a gap that our veterans will have to fill as a group.”
Fortunately, Buckhannon-Upshur returns no shortage of experienced playmakers ready to embrace more responsibility on both sides of the ball.
Set to lead the charge on the 41-player roster will be a collection of 15 seniors, headlined by team-elected captains Kadyn Baisden, Jacob Frye, Greyson Wyland and Tobias Marple.
“We did a team vote this season and our players voted our captains, which is a process that I feel gives the players ownership and puts the most respected players in those spots,” coach Baisden said. “In that same breath, we had a couple more guys like Easton Metzner, Eli Watkins and Gage Scott who pulled votes too, which really speaks to the depth of that senior class.”
Kadyn Baisden’s selection follows a standout campaign in which he emerged as an ironman stalwart at center while anchoring the defense at linebacker, earning first-team All-Big 10 Blue Division and second-team Class AAAA All-State honors behind a team-high 110 tackles, including 11 tackles for loss or sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery.
“It’s an honor for my teammates to recognize me as a leader,” Kadyn Baisden said. “It’s a responsibility I don’t take lightly and I’ll continue to do all I can to put us in a position to win this season.”
Frye’s election reflects his status as one of the Buccaneers’ most proven offensive weapons after hauling in 46 receptions for a school-record 892 yards and nine touchdowns a year ago.
“Being named a captain means the world to me,” Frye said. “I’m going to give my all to prove those that have trusted me to be a leader right by uplifting others and setting an example for our younger players to follow.”
Wyland’s recognition was earned through his impactful presence around the line of scrimmage, especially on defense, where he collected All-Big 10 Blue Division honors after recording 75 tackles, including nine stops behind the line last season.
Rounding out the quartet, Marple embodies the physical, hard-nosed style Buckhannon-Upshur wants to carry onto the field through tireless preparation, hustle and a willingness to embrace the demands of playing in the trenches.
Beyond the four captains, Buckhannon-Upshur returns a deep offensive arsenal, which coach Baisden points to as a particular strength of this year’s team.
“Picking the strongest aspect of this team is difficult, but I’d probably go with our skill position groups. We’ve got a great group of athletes,” coach Baisden said. “There’s a solid mix of proven returners and exciting new additions that can make an impact.”
Taking over the reins of the offense will be Brody McDaniels, who returns to the gridiron after spending the past few years focused on basketball and baseball, with Xavier Robinette working behind him at quarterback.
McDaniels will have an established duo of targets to lean on in Frye and Robinette, while Forest Catlin, Aidan Squires, Easton Metzner and Logen Michael will provide further big-play potential out wide.
The rushing attack holds similar promise, with Chance Morgan, Alex Wamsley, Levi Cook and Angelo Dues forming a versatile collection of threats out of the backfield.
However, question marks linger up front following the graduation of Garrett Cutright and Conner McKim, with Caiden Keener and Jude Snider among those expected to assume larger roles after gaining valuable varsity experience as freshmen a year ago.
“I loved seeing Caiden and Jude step up last season,” coach Baisden said. “They made the most of their varsity opportunities in their first season and will take on bigger roles anchoring the line of scrimmage this season.”
The team’s season-long progression up front will prove critical for a group that wants to place physicality at the heart of its identity.
Nowhere will that emphasis be more apparent than on defense, where the Buccaneers want their grit to dictate the terms of each opposing possession.
“I expect our defense to be aggressive and never stop coming from the opening snap,” Kadyn Baisden said. “We have a chip on our shoulder and we want teams to know they’re going to have to work for everything when they line up against us.”
Buckhannon-Upshur will couple that relentless mentality with a disciplined approach designed to keep opposing offenses off balance.
“Defensively, we want to be fundamentally sound, fly around and force offenses into tough situations,” coach Baisden said. “Our goal is to control the pace of the game, limit big plays and make opponents operate on our terms.”
Aiden Snyder, a talented kicker and punter capable of impacting field position and putting points on the board, leads a sound special teams unit.
With the pieces falling into place across all three phases, Buckhannon-Upshur now turns its attention toward putting its potential into action and seeing where it can lead.
“Our expectations never change because we define success as getting better at football every single day,” coach Baisden said. “We always let effort lead the way. If we play smart, play fast and are confident in what we are doing, then good things will happen.”
The Buccaneers will put their improvement to the test when they open the season on the road against Bridgeport on Friday, Aug. 28, at 7 p.m.
